decisions.quote: All in all, our research findings in Rotterdam refute the general claim by Leisering and Leibfried, and in their footstep Beck and Giddens, that most contemporary poverty is of a temporary nature. Unfortunately, persistent poverty is still present in our age and in our cities.
decisions.location: Discussion, p. 11 (lines 1563-1572); see also Abstract, p. 1 (lines 86-90)
decisions.reason: Under Rule 1 of the codebook, where the authors state an overall verdict on how the replication came out as a whole, that verdict decides the outcome even when individual comparisons point elsewhere. Both tested main claims regarding the temporalization of poverty (spell duration) and recurrent benefit spells failed to replicate, and in both the Abstract ('Leisering and Leibfried (and sociologists such as Giddens and Beck in their footsteps) are wrong in claiming that short poverty experiences are typical for poverty in late-modern society') and the Discussion ('The differences between our research findings and theirs were striking... All in all, our research findings in Rotterdam refute the general claim by Leisering and Leibfried... In Rotterdam... we come to very different outcomes'), the authors state an unambiguous overall verdict of failure. Partial agreement on background demographic covariates in an exploratory multivariate regression of spell duration does not override the authors' explicit overall verdict on the replication as a whole.
